page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.se1ne family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance features 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, reaching 654.2 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 75.3 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

Given its memory-to-vCPU ratio and performance profile, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. It achieves average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations at 11.19 million operations per second, and static web serving. It is also capable of handling moderate multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation and small-scale LLM inference, though performance drops significantly on larger models. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a qualitative choice for memory-heavy, non-accelerated workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation.
